hook: Context is the scarcest resource in every agent system. Four disciplines — **compaction, selective retrieval, budget planning, memory safety** — that keep long runs coherent.

scenes.title: Compaction: summarize the past, **keep the present**
scenes.sub: How long sessions survive finite windows
scenes.narration: Compaction is the garbage collector of agent memory: as context fills, old turns are REPLACED by a running summary — 'turns one through twenty, compressed: user asked X, we tried Y, found Z, open questions: …'. The detail is gone; the STATE survives. Done well, compaction preserves exactly what future steps need: decisions made, constraints agreed, artifacts produced with their locations, and open threads — the facts that change what the agent should DO next. Done badly — a lazy 'previous work happened' summary — the agent loses the plot while appearing fine. The trigger discipline: compact BEFORE the window is full, on task boundaries or at a usage threshold — seventy percent say — not in a panic at ninety-nine, and keep the last few turns VERBATIM: recent exchanges are the working set, and summarizing them buys amnesia at the exact moment it's most expensive.

scenes.title: What a good compaction preserves
scenes.body:
# Running Summary (turns 1–20 compressed)

## Decisions
- User chose DuckDB over pandas for the analytics path (speed, zero-install).

## Constraints
- All writes must go through the MCP excel server (AG-09 guardrails).
- Budget: < $5 of API spend for this whole task.

## Artifacts (paths, not contents)
- research notes: /runs/7/notes.md (scratchpad)
- competitor list: /runs/7/competitors.csv

## Open threads
- Q: email the summary to finance? — awaiting user answer
- The Acme pricing is from a cached page; needs re-fetching

## Do NOT re-derive
- The 5-report migration order was already validated by the user.
annot: Decisions + constraints are the load-bearing content — losing them changes future behavior
Artifacts by PATH: contents live in scratchpad files (AG-12); the summary stores pointers, not payloads
'Do NOT re-derive' stops the post-compaction agent from re-litigating settled questions — the classic compaction bug
scenes.narration: The structure IS the lesson: decisions, constraints, artifact pointers, open threads — four categories, each answering 'what would change my next action?'. What gets dropped by design: intermediate reasoning, failed attempts already learned from, raw tool outputs superseded by their results. A second compaction technique: hierarchical summaries — when the summary itself grows long, summarize the summary, keeping the most recent section detailed — the same rolling structure as GA-14's episode compression. And the verification habit: after compacting, a cheap check — 'state three constraints from your summary' — catches a bad compaction while recovery is still cheap, instead of fifty turns later when the damage is baked into every artifact.

scenes.title: Don't load memory — **query** it
scenes.sub: Only what's needed, when it's needed
scenes.narration: The anti-pattern: dumping all long-term memory into every session 'for context'. A thousand memories injected at start buys three things: cost, distraction, and silent relevance failures — the model attends to a vivid-but-wrong memory while the right one sits unretrieved. Selective retrieval is Stage 4's craft applied inward: embed the CURRENT task, search memory for matches, inject the top few WITH their provenance metadata; retrieve at the moment of need, not just at session start — mid-task, when the agent hits the database layer, THAT'S when database-related memories should surface. And support the second recall path from AG-12: situation-based episodic recall — 'tasks like this one' — as a separate search over episode summaries. Memory retrieval quality degrades exactly the way RAG retrieval does: measure it, golden-set it, and distrust it the same way.

items.s: Embed the current task/step · inject top-k matches only · provenance attached (recency, confidence)
Retrieve at the moment of need — database memories surface when touching the database
Forced recall injects confident noise · abstain when similarity is thin

scenes.narration: The abstention point transfers directly from GA-16: a memory system that always returns SOMETHING will eventually return the wrong thing confidently, and a wrong memory in context is worse than no memory — it contradicts reality with authority. Set a similarity threshold; below it, the agent proceeds memoryless and notes the gap. Also design for CONFLICT: retrieval may surface two memories that disagree — 'deploys from main' and 'deploys from a release branch' — the injection layer should detect the contradiction and prefer by provenance — recency, confidence — or surface it honestly to the user rather than silently picking. Memory quality is retrieval quality: chunk well, tag well, measure recall against known cases, and version the store like the golden dataset it is.

scenes.title: Context budget planning: **every token has a job**
scenes.narration: A context window is a budget, and unplanned budgets get spent on trivia. The allocation discipline: reserve the SYSTEM PROMPT first — instructions, tool schemas — it's fixed cost; then a memory allowance — the retrieved top-k, capped; then the working conversation — recent turns verbatim; then tool OUTPUT quotas — the actual budget-buster: a fetch of a hundred-kilobyte page or a five-thousand-row query result can consume a third of the window in one observation. Tool outputs need caps by design — truncation with continuation pointers, 'result stored at path, summary follows' — AG-12's scratchpad pattern as a context-saving device. Plan for the WORST turn: the step where everything is needed at once — if the plan doesn't fit the window at its fullest moment, the plan doesn't fit, period; redesign before the failure, not at it.

layers.s: Fixed cost — know it exactly · counts against every single call
Capped top-k · provenance attached · abstention below threshold
Recent verbatim · older compacted (ch. 1) · headroom reserved for the reply
Per-tool byte caps · summarize-or-store · continuation pointers

scenes.narration: The four layers, in priority order — and notice the ordering logic: fixed costs first, then the highest-leverage variable costs, then the working set, with output quotas as the shock absorber. Two planning exercises pay off immediately. Instrument FIRST: log tokens per layer per call in development — most teams discover their tool outputs are eating half the window, invisible until measured. And reserve reply headroom: the model's response, including its next tool-call arguments, needs room — systems that fill the window with INPUT leave the model room for a truncated, broken OUTPUT — the malformed JSON tool-call that breaks the loop. Budget planning feels like accounting because it is: the agents that run long aren't the ones with bigger windows — they're the ones spending smaller windows deliberately.

scenes.title: Memory safety: **some things must never be stored**
scenes.sub: PII, secrets, and the consent boundary
scenes.narration: Memory systems are dangerous in a specific way: they PERSIST. A secret typed once in a chat, if written to long-term memory, is a secret stored forever, replicated across backups, retrieved into unknown future contexts. The safety rules. Never store: credentials and secrets — the memory layer should run a secret-scanner at write time — the same redaction discipline as logging; PII — names, emails, health data — without a purpose and consent basis — regulation treats stored personal data seriously regardless of where it's stored, and 'the agent remembered it' is not a defense; and unverified claims marked as facts — the 'unverified' label from AG-12 isn't pedantry; recalled as fact, a rumor becomes policy. Add the secondary boundary: retrieved memories enter the context of FUTURE tasks, including tasks with different users or permissions — memory is a cross-session information flow, and flows need access checks, not just write discipline.

items.s: Detect keys/tokens before they persist — memory's write gate is a security boundary
Purpose + consent basis before storing personal data · per-user memory scoping
Memories cross sessions — retrieve only what the CURRENT user/task may see

scenes.narration: The per-user scoping point is the one most personal-agent designs miss: a memory store shared across users must scope retrieval by user the way GA-17 scoped retrieval by ACL — 'what did the user tell us' is per-user information, and one user's memories surfacing in another's session is a privacy incident with a fancy name. Practical pattern: memory namespaces per user per domain, with the retrieval filter mandatory, not optional — the same where-clause discipline as filtered vector search. And audit memory like you audit anything else that persists: what's stored, who can recall it, what was evicted — because the day someone asks 'show me everything the system remembers about me', the only good answer is a query, not a shrug. Memory is the most permanent component of your agent — treat permanence as a risk as well as a feature.

scenes.title: One agent's context, mastered. Now several agents, orchestrated.
scenes.next: Reel 56 · Architectures — supervisors, handoffs, blackboards, A2A

recap: Compaction preserves decisions, constraints, artifact pointers and open threads — triggered early, keeping recent turns verbatim
Retrieve memory just-in-time with task anchors and thresholds; 'no memory' is a valid answer; conflicts resolved by provenance
Budget every token: instrument layers, cap tool outputs, reserve reply headroom; never persist secrets or unscoped PII

quiz.q: What must a compaction summary preserve to be useful?
opts: Decisions, constraints, artifact paths, open threads — the content that changes future actions
quiz.why: Compaction's test: can the agent continue correctly? Only state-changing facts answer that — payloads belong in files, pointed to.

quiz.q: Why is 'dump all memory at session start' an anti-pattern?
opts: Cost, distraction, and false confidence — uncurated injection buries the right memory under vivid wrong ones
quiz.why: Selective, just-in-time retrieval with thresholds serves relevance; bulk injection serves the illusion of context.

quiz.q: Why does memory need access checks at RETRIEVAL time, not just write discipline?
opts: Memories cross sessions and users — a per-user fact surfacing in another user's session is a privacy incident
quiz.why: Memory is an information flow across contexts; flows need scoping at both ends — the ACL-filter lesson of GA-17, applied inward.

code.title: The context budget, enforced in one wrapper
code.body:
BUDGET = {
    "system":  None,     # measured, fixed
    "memory":  2_000,    # tokens, retrieved top-k cap
    "recent":  8_000,    # verbatim turns
    "reserve": 4_000,    # reply + next tool-call headroom
}

async def build_context(state, task, user):
    ctx = [system_prompt(), tool_schemas()]              # fixed

    mems = memory.search(embed(task), k=4,               # selective
                         where={"user": user.id},        # access-checked
                         min_score=0.82)                  # abstain below
    ctx += format_memories(mems)[:BUDGET["memory"]]

    ctx += recent_turns(state, token_cap=BUDGET["recent"])
    if usage(ctx) > WINDOW - BUDGET["reserve"]:
        ctx = compact(ctx, keep_recent=3)                # ch.1 discipline
    return ctx

# Tool outputs are capped INSIDE each tool (AG-02): summarize-or-store,
# return pointer + summary. The wrapper never sees raw monsters.
annot: The where-clause on memory search is the GA-17 ACL filter — non-negotiable, not a feature flag
min_score encodes 'no memory is an answer' — thin similarity returns nothing instead of noise
The reserve is sacred: an input-stuffed window produces truncated, malformed outputs

notes:
# Context Management

## Compaction
- Replace old turns with running summary: decisions · constraints · artifact paths · open threads.
- Trigger early (not at 99%), keep recent verbatim, verify ('state three constraints').

## Selective retrieval
- Task-anchored, just-in-time, top-k with thresholds; abstain when thin.
- Detect conflicts by provenance; measure recall like RAG.

## Budget planning
- Layers: system+tools (fixed) · memory cap · recent verbatim · reply reserve.
- Tool output quotas: summarize-or-store with pointers.
- Instrument per layer; plan for the worst turn.

## Memory safety
- No secrets/PII persisted (secret-scan at write; consent basis).
- 'Unverified' ≠ fact. Per-user namespacing; retrieval-time access checks.
